questions.question: What is the European Union (EU)? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• The European Union is a group of European countries that cooperate economically and
  • politically, allowing free movement of goods, services, capital, and people among member
  • states.

questions.question: Mention any two benefits of FTAs. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Reduction or elimination of tariffs, Increased market access, Boost to exports, Lower prices
  • for consumers, Encouragement of foreign investment, Improved efficiency and competitiveness.

questions.question: Define resource efficiency? How does it helps in export? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Resource efficiency means using natural resources in a sustainable and optimal way with
  • minimal waste.
  • It helps exports by:
  • Reducing production costs and improving competitiveness in international markets

questions.question: What is the role of financial services in India’s exports. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Financial services support exports by:
  • Providing trade finance (loans, credit), facilitating international payments and
  • managing risks through insurance and hedging

questions.question: Who maintains foreign exchange reserves? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • In India, the Reserve Bank of India maintains foreign exchange reserves.

questions.question: How do wars affect foreign trade of countries? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Wars disrupt trade by:
  • Damaging infrastructure, increasing transport costs and risks, causing supply chain disruptions
  • and leading to trade restrictions or sanctions

questions.question: What is meant by non-tariff barriers? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Non-tariff barriers are restrictions other than tariffs used to control imports, such as quotas,
  • licenses, and quality standards.

questions.question: How does export trade affect foreign exchange? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Exports bring foreign currency into a country, increasing its foreign exchange reserves and
  • strengthening its balance of payments.

questions.question: What is the current account in Balance of Payments? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• The current account records a country’s transactions related to:
  • Trade in goods and services, Income (interest, dividends) and Transfers (remittances, aid)

questions.question: What is trade deficit? / [CO4]
questions.solution_html: • A trade deficit occurs when a country’s imports exceed its exports.

questions.question: Why are SDGs important for developing countries? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are important because they:
  • • Promote economic growth and poverty reduction
  • • Encourage sustainable use of resources
  • • Improve health, education, and living standards

questions.question: What is a Preferential Trade Area (PTA)? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• A PTA is a trade agreement where member countries give preferential (reduced) tariffs to
  • each other but do not eliminate them completely.

questions.question: Describe the differences between General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade and General Agreement on Trade in Services. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GA TT) and the General Agreement on Trade in
  • Services differ in several key aspects. GA TT, established in 1947, focuses on the promotion of
  • international trade in goods and mainly covers physical products such as manufactured items and
  • raw materials. In contrast, GA TS, introduced in 1995, deals with trade in services, including
  • sectors like banking, information technology, and tourism. While GA TT aims at reducing tariffs
  • and barriers on goods, GA TS provides a framework for liberalizing and regulating global trade in
  • services.

questions.question: What are the reasons for India's reliance on imported crude oil? / [CO4] [2x10 = 20]
questions.solution_html:
• Reasons for India's reliance on imported crude oil:
  • Limited domestic oil production, high and growing energy demand, rapid industrialization and
  • urbanization and lack of sufficient alternative energy sources

questions.question: Explain India’s major trade partners and their role in foreign trade. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• India’s major trade partners include the United States, China, United Arab Emirates, Saudi
  • Arabia, and the European Union.
  • Role in foreign trade:
  • • United States: Major destination for IT services, pharmaceuticals, and textiles
  • • China: Key supplier of machinery, electronics, and raw materials
  • • UAE: Important hub for oil trade, gold imports, and re-exports
  • • Saudi Arabia: Major source of crude oil imports
  • • EU: Large market for engineering goods, automobiles, and garments
  • These partners help India diversify trade, ensure energy security, and expand export markets

questions.question: Analyse the shift in India’s export composition toward high-value sectors. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• India’s exports have shifted from traditional goods (like agriculture and textiles) to high-
  • value sectors such as:
  • IT and software services, Pharmaceuticals, Engineering goods, Electronics
  • Reasons for the shift: Technological advancement, Skilled workforce availability, Government
  • initiatives like “Make in India”, Global demand for services
  • Impact:
  • Higher export earnings, improved global competitiveness, reduced dependence on low-value
  • exports

questions.question: Explain the concept of free trade and protectionism with examples. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Free trade is a system in which countries exchange goods and services without significant
  • restrictions such as tariffs, quotas, or import bans. It promotes open markets and allows
  • countries to specialize based on their comparative advantage. For example, under rules of the
  • World Trade Organization, many countries reduce tariffs to encourage global trade.
  • Protectionism, on the other hand, refers to government policies that restrict imports to protect
  • domestic industries from foreign competition. These measures include tariffs, quotas, subsidies,
  • and import restrictions. For example, a country may impose high import duties on foreign steel
  • to protect its local steel industry.

questions.question: Discuss the differences between domestic and international trade in terms of scope and operation. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Domestic trade refers to trade that takes place within a country, while international trade
  • occurs between different countries.
  • In domestic trade, the same currency is used, whereas international trade involves different
  • currencies.
  • Domestic trade is subject to fewer restrictions and simpler regulations, while international trade
  • requires compliance with more complex legal formalities and customs procedures.
  • Transport in domestic trade is generally easier, faster, and cheaper, whereas in international trade
  • it is more complex and costly due to long distances and logistics.
  • Finally, domestic trade involves lower risk, while international trade carries higher risk due to
  • factors such as exchange rate fluctuations and political instability.

questions.question: Explain the meaning and objectives of Free Trade Agreements in detail. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Meaning:
  • FTAs are agreements between countries to reduce or eliminate trade barriers like tariffs and
  • quotas.
  • Objectives:
  • Promote international trade, increase market access, encourage investment flows, enhance
  • economic cooperation, reduce cost of goods for consumers and Improve efficiency and
  • competitiveness.

questions.question: What is CBAM? Discuss key aspects of CBAM? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) is a policy introduced by the European
  • Union to impose carbon costs on imports based on their carbon emissions.
  • Key aspects:
  • • Applies to carbon-intensive products (steel, cement, etc.)
  • • Prevents “carbon leakage” (shifting production to countries with lax climate rules)
  • • Encourages cleaner production globally
  • • Importers must report emissions and may pay carbon charges

questions.question: Analyse role of technology in foreign trade. / [CO3] [5x3 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Technology plays a crucial role in modern trade:
  • • Digital platforms enable global e-commerce
  • • Blockchain improves transparency and reduces fraud
  • • Automation & AI enhance production efficiency
  • • Digital payments speed up international transactions
  • • Logistics technology improves supply chain management
  • Impact:
  • • Reduces transaction costs
  • • Increases speed and efficiency
